proof.text:
Let $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a nonempty open subset and choose a prime point $\mathfrak p\in U$. By the basic-open basis for affine spectra, there is an element $f\in A$ with $f
otin\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak p\in D(f)\subseteq U$. Apply the prime-containing-minimal-prime lemma to the ideal $(0)\subseteq\mathfrak p$ to obtain a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A$ with $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Since $f
otin\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$, also $f
otin\mathfrak q$, so the point $\mathfrak q$ lies in $D(f)\subseteq U$. Thus every nonempty open contains a minimal-prime point, which is exactly density.

title: Minimal primes are dense in the spectrum
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a commutative finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. In the Zariski space $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the set of points corresponding to minimal prime ideals of $A$ is dense: every nonempty open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ contains a minimal prime point.
